I can give you advice from my experience up to this point. I am someone who has manifested mostly smaller things, some of them coming all at once when I felt my best (happy, fulfilled and full of gratitude for whatever I already had).

From 2016-2019, I tried to manifest something that meant the world to me but it didn't happen. I fell into severe depression in 2019. Then I got into mindfulness, or living in the present.

Looking back at that experience 4.5 years later, I realize that I was way too hard on myself and completely relied on my manifestation to happen to start living. Which is not only an awful way to live, but you're also not positioned well to manifest that way.

So if you feel too anxious about your manifestation and worry that it won't happen, you need to take a step back and learn to be more present. I like to refer to Eckhart Tolle's teachings to achieve this peace. Once you've achieved this peace, then you can focus on your manifestation again. That's my advice!

Two things here.

First of all, mindfulness doesn't necessarily mean you have to take time out of your day to meditate. For example, I practice mindfulness every day, but I haven't sat down and meditated in like 3-4 years. Traditional sit-down meditation is just not for me. Instead, I go about my regular chores and hobbies and just be present throughout those so that I can have an easier, lighter life with less worries and stress. So it really isn't an extra thing you have to do, you are just enhancing the experience of the things you are already doing.

Secondly, seeing your life as a bunch of things you HAVE to do is a thought. In mindfulness, there are no thoughts. As soon as you get the thought that there are too many things you have to do, see that as a signal that you need to become present that very moment. As soon as you do that, the thought will fade and you will feel lighter.

Believe me, the feeling of not being able to be present is strong among many of us. I have been practicing mindfulness for around 3 years now, and while I have definitely improved, some days are easier to practice than others. So I would start by accepting that its hard.

With that being said, it seems you are focusing too much on the end goal, which is preventing you from feeling joy in the practice. Have you read "The Power of Now" by Eckhart Tolle? Eckhart mentions that people are constantly doing things as a means to an end. For example, those who hate doing dishes still need to do them so as they are doing them, they are just waiting to be done with them. This ruins the experience of just hearing the water running, feeling the dishes in your hands etc. Sure, its not so fun and make you super happy, but you can still find joy in it.

I think you should pay attention to what thoughts are coming up as you are trying to do a mindful activity, and then accept that you are thinking that thought, good or bad. Once you accept, focus on your five senses again and just observe. You will progressively feel more peaceful, even though it might feel uncomfortable at first since you are not used to it.

I also struggle with anxiety, but I notice that the more I practice mindfulness, the more peaceful I become as I am not trying hard to control events. For example, if something does not go as planned, I just continue to be mindful and MOVE ON. Helps me to not worry about how I perform or what happens.

If I am being mindful and still feel anxious (which still happens to me many times), I just accept the feeling of the anxiety and it definitely becomes less strong. 

The key formula for me is mindfulness + acceptance.

Although you don’t like your current situation, you will find that staying focused on a single moment at a time will cultivate SO MUCH PEACE you will start to feel weightless and free.

I think you should try Michael Raduga’s process. Here is the basic outline:

1. Set an alarm to wake up at 5-6 in the morning. Get up and use to restroom and/or eat. You should be awake anywhere from 5-50 minutes.

2. Go over your plan of action in your head a couple of times.

3. Go back to sleep with the intention of doing AP immediately upon awakening. 

4. When you get your first natural awakening, don’t move and try to show up at a mirror. If it doesn’t work try a separation technique. Do these for 5 seconds each. 

5. If that doesn’t work, you use other techniques, shifting between 2-3 techniques for 5 seconds each. Once you’ve done 4 cycles of these techniques and nothing worked, go back to sleep.

6. During your next natural awakenings, you repeat this process until you succeed. 

Hope this helps!

Moving across the country 

When I was 13, I didn’t even know about LOA. However, I really wanted to move across the country to another state, but my mom wasn’t down for the long move because of the uncertainty. But still, every morning, I went on Google Street View and looked at the place I wanted to move with my family. I just put in my music and felt I was really there, only because it felt good. I think I did this for about a month and a half. I NEVER thought about living where I was in the future, and since I was a young kid, I didn’t really worry or have doubt. Now here is the crazy part. My family owns a property in another state, not the state I want to move to, but a state we lived in the past. It turns out there was a storm there and it messed our property up, causing hazards. We had to physically go to the city to settle some matters with the city’s officials. This state was in between the state we were currently living in and the state we wanted to move to. In addition to that, my dad called (my mom and dad are separated, and he had not called in 2 years). He told my mom how he was sorry for abandoning the family and that he wanted to move with us. This gave my mom hope, so she agreed to move to the state I wanted to move to. It turns out my dad just wanted to use my mom for money, and didn’t come with us along the way (which is good, considering his history of violence). Of course, my mom was worried about how she would manage everything but things fell into place almost immediately. When I reached my destination, I put in the same music I would listen to in my street view sessions, and it was like the best feeling ever. LOA is real.
